## 1. What was read

**865 research articles** from 33 of the 33 journals on the roster.

A further **291** records (25% of the 1,156 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. Every count below is over the full harvest and is inflated by this; the figure above is not.

| General | Cancer | Immune | Bioinfo | Sysbio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 516 | 208 | 89 | 312 | 31 |

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: sysbio +29%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). Every journal on the roster contributed this month. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nature 123, JAMA 115, Nucleic Acids Res 94, Science 84, Bioinformatics 74, Lancet 64.

## 3. The evidence that moved it






**The strongest month for foundation-model refutations in the corpus, and the
form has changed.** Five cards, and four of them replace the model with a
trivial baseline and watch the number stay put: classical molecular fingerprints
with shallow classifiers [match or beat protein language models](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41981726/) on
peptide function; ML and deep survival models
[fail to beat Cox baselines](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41992491/) on low-dimensional clinical data;
structure-aware substitution models built on predicted structures
[do not improve on plain sequence models](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42036821/); and
[scArchon](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42121287/) shows deep perturbation-response predictors fail to
beat trivial baselines on held-out perturbations. The fifth,
[42020757](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42020757/) (*Nature*), is about the scoring rather than the model:
accuracy-scored LLM benchmarks reward confident fabrication rather than
measuring truthfulness.

**ctDNA took two more hits, one of them a landmark.**
[41817436](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41817436/) (*Cancer Discov*) reports that the GRAIL Galleri
multi-cancer early detection trial did not deliver the expected mortality or
stage-shift evidence, and [TOMBOLA](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41544704/) finds ctDNA-triggered
atezolizumab after cystectomy does not deliver the anticipated relapse control.
With [41616224](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41616224/) on tumour-naive MRD underperformance, the thread
now reads: ctDNA detects reliably, and acting on the detection has yet to
demonstrate benefit in a randomized setting outside nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

**Anti-TIGIT got a defence rather than a result.** [41564381](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41564381/)
(*JCO*) argues the first generation of anti-TIGIT antibodies failed on Fc isotype
design, meaning the target was never properly tested. This is a specific,
falsifiable claim rather than special pleading, and it is the kind of argument
that decides whether `next-gen-checkpoints` gets reopened or stays closed. Note
its structure: the same manoeuvre — the target survives by relocating the blame
to the format — has now been applied to CD47, TIGIT and CTLA-4 in this corpus.

**Interception found its causal variable.** [41781610](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41781610/) (*Nature*)
reports that precancerous **niche remodelling, not the mutant clone**, gates
whether nascent tumours persist. Read with February's three papers dissolving
the single-clone precursor model, the field has spent 2026 moving the unit of
interception from the cell to the tissue.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[41701973](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41701973/) (*Blood*): time of infusion does not affect CAR-T
outcomes in large B-cell lymphoma. This is a clean null on a chrono-immunology
hypothesis that a 2025 card had supported for allogeneic transplant, and it is
recorded here precisely because the corpus should not accumulate only the
positive half of a fashionable idea.

### (b) Method credibility

Four cards, and two of them are about the physical instrument or the animal
rather than the software. [42133765](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42133765/) (*Science*): mouse-line
genetic quality control is inadequate, and unmonitored drift is a hidden
artifact behind irreproducible phenotypes. [41882360](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41882360/) (*Nature*):
DNA supercoiling drives Cas9 off-target cleavage that standard specificity
assays cannot see — the third editing-safety card in seven months, after
November's [heritable impairment after repair](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41196998/) and December's
[epigenetic disruption by double-strand breaks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41331675/).

[42141119](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42141119/) (*Nat Biotechnol*): DNA off-targeting confounds
RNA-chromatin occupancy assays, making a body of published RNA-chromatin maps
artifactual. [42129548](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42129548/) (*Nat Methods*): analysis results shift
with software package choice and version — the second month in a row with that
finding, after April's [41903535](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41903535/), now from a different journal
and a different data modality.

The pattern across April and May is worth naming. The audit genre spent 2025
moving from the model to the pipeline to the instrument. In 2026 it has arrived
at **the version number** — the claim is no longer that a method is wrong, but
that the same method on the same data gives a different answer depending on when
you ran it.
